inlineScriptHashesNote: NOT LISTED HERE, AND MEASURED RATHER THAN OMITTED: across two builds of one commit (this machine and a fresh clone of 80e3223) four of the six hashes were identical and exactly two differed — the RSC payload pushes carry build-specific content. A committed hash list would therefore be wrong on every machine but the one that wrote it, which `tools/gate/bin/fresh-clone-proof` proved as a CI step within the hour. The consequence for Task 12 is the useful part: a script-src policy for this page CANNOT be static — it must be emitted by the build from that build’s own output, or by the edge as a per-response nonce. `build-surface.test.ts` computes the hashes on every run and asserts their count and shape, so the capability is proven without pinning a build artefact.
note: The scan landing carries the raw QR token in its URL fragment, so any script on this origin can read it. That is why clause (b) of PLAN §3 row 9 is asserted against the build and why clause (c) wants a policy that makes it impossible.
